Health lovers can go for fresh sprouts and refreshing cold-pressed juices, while foodies can happily indulge in cheesy pizzas, loaded burgers, and grilled sandwiches. Got a sweet tooth? Was here for a night at Mumbai due to my transit to west Africa. Was just curious and started to walk from my hotel which was nearby.

featured_reviews.name: yash Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely disappointing experience at Amar Juice, Marol. The food quality was genuinely poor and far below expectations. The pav served with pav bhaji was cold, and even the idli and dosa did not feel fresh or properly prepared.The worst part was the salad & curd — it tasted bitter and seemed old, almost like it was prepared a day earlier. When this issue was raised with the manager, instead of resolving the complaint professionally, the response given was: “Sir humare yaha aisa hi milta hai.” Completely unacceptable customer service.
Another shocking thing I personally experienced was the difference in quality and service between AC and non-AC customers. Due to overcrowding in the AC section, I had to sit outside in the non-AC area, and it was clearly noticeable that different quality food was being served there compared to inside. This kind of discrimination towards customers is highly disappointing. Also, many people may confuse this place with the famous Amar Juice near Mithibai College, but this outlet is NOT associated with that original brand. Using a similar name while delivering such poor quality only damages the goodwill that the original Amar Juice has built over many years.
I would definitely not recommend this place to anyone to visit on any occassion based on my experiences.

featured_reviews.name: Tariq Theba
featured_reviews.review_text:
I'm extremely disappointed with my recent experience with Kurla Juice Hut's Jogeshwari West branch. I ordered two veg melting sandwiches, which took an astonishing 1 hour and 20 minutes to arrive, despite being only 2.5 km away from my location.

The sandwiches themselves were a letdown. They were not fresh, not warm, and seemed to have been prepared long before my order. To make matters worse, they were excessively salty, rendering them inedible.

What's more, the order was incomplete, as they forgot to include the usual accompaniments of chutney and mayonnaise.

I tried to report the issue to Zomato support, but they claimed they couldn't validate the issue with the restaurant.

To add insult to injury, when I called the restaurant to inform them about the issue, they disconnected the call twice, without even bothering to listen to my concerns.

I've been a loyal customer of Kurla Juice Hut's Kurla branch in the past, but this experience has left a sour taste. The service has clearly deteriorated since the opening of this new branch.

Unless they seriously revamp their quality control, delivery, and customer service, I would strongly advise against ordering from this branch.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Khopade
featured_reviews.review_text:
Confession: I literally had to Google what to order before stepping in here. I am not a coffee snob at all, but the crazy social media hype finally pulled me in, and sach batau, I completely get the obsession now.
I started with a black Pour Over. It is definitely an acquired taste, but it really grows on you. My second visit was the real game changer when I tried their Cold Brew with milk. It is not your basic cafe cold coffee. They carefully pour the milk over iced black coffee almost like a cocktail, and it is absolutely brilliant.
The space itself is huge and perfectly located near business hubs. It is the ultimate spot for people watching. You have folks closing corporate deals, students chilling, and creatives buried in their laptops.
You can easily kill a few hours here just soaking in the energy without anyone bothering you. Grab a table, keep the coffee coming, and enjoy the vibe. Definitely worth the hype.

I recently visited Blue Tokai Cafe and had mixed feelings about the experience. I am a regular customer of Blue Tokai, which is why this visit was especially disappointing. The cheesecake was genuinely delicious, fresh and creamy, and easily the highlight of my visit.

It is unfortunate because the food and coffee are usually good, but the way staff are treated and how customers witness that behavior really affects the overall experience. I hope they work on creating a more respectful and professional environment.

Special thanks to Miss. Khushboo and Mr. Robin (Bombay to Barcelona cafe team members) for there efficiency in serving the orders at peak hours of rush.

featured_reviews.name: Debarshi Datta
featured_reviews.review_text: Brilliant place and a must visit if you are nearby! Was there for brunch on the LP/Lolla day, so was quite busy but I feel they managed it really well. Food and staff were both really good. Would definitely have gone back there if I had more time in Mumbai. Their back story is also very interesting, so do try and find out about that!

featured_reviews.name: Niyati Singhvi
featured_reviews.review_text: This place stands out with its unconventional concept of combining a library and café, creating a cozy and relaxed vibe that’s perfect for unwinding. It’s easy to locate and has a warm, inviting atmosphere. The Nutella melted pancakes are a highlight—not just delicious but also creatively presented in cute shapes. The Malta Mojito is refreshing, and the Café Bonbon is definitely worth trying. The toasted garlic bread, however, is skippable. The space isn’t ideal for large groups, but it’s a great spot for a quick outing. Overall, definitely recommended for a visit.

featured_reviews.name: D M
featured_reviews.review_text:
If I were to rate the cafe's concept, it would be a 5! But if you ask me about my overall experience, it will be strictly a 3.

The ambience is bang on perfect for hanging out with friends. There are books stacked like a mini library which you can read while you enjoy a bite. The food that we tried was so not great though. We tried:

•White sauce chicken pasta
•Chicken B2BLC sandwich
•Cold coffee with almond milk (of which the almond milk quantity was only available for 1 serve. Disappointing.)
•Cold coffee with hazelnut
•Paneer pesto crepe
•Chicken fingers

Overall, the pasta was the winner. It was cooked very well with the sauce tasting creamy and delicious. It was served with the normal bread cut into triangles and toasted. The sandwich size was quite huge with a good amount of filling. Not at all a fan of both the cold coffees - One with almond milk and the other with cow milk. The paneer pesto wrap didn’t have salt and the taste was quite off and not balanced. It’s supposed to be creamy but instead we could taste only the greens. It was a total letdown. The crepe covering was nice though but again what’s the point? Chicken fingers seemed a bit over-fried and stale served with a sauce (it was definitely not mayonnaise as told to us) which did not go well. We chose not to eat all 6 pieces as a result.

The service was alright. The server made a face when we could not finish everything on the plate and commented that it would be given to someone else. Now I understand that’s very noble of them to do that to prevent food wastage. I politely replied on the same lines with a smile. His tone seemed rude nor were there any other mannerisms leaving us baffled and uncomfortable.

Overall not a great experience and would skip returning.

featured_reviews.name: Prajakta Chorge
featured_reviews.review_text: The staff members are very welcoming. I enjoyed the cafe bonbon; it is quite good if you appreciate a strong coffee. I truly love both the place and its ambiance. I would highly recommend it for meeting with friends and it's also a wonderful spot for book lovers.

featured_reviews.name: Pranay Hegde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bombay to Barcelona is a must-visit café if you’re in Mumbai!
The food here is amazing and the vibe is just perfect. Absolutely loved the paneer pesto sandwich and the coffees are really good too .
But the best thing above all? The staff and their service—truly top knotch.
If you’re here, don’t miss reading about the team and the owner who are building this beautiful place. Their story makes the experience even more special.

featured_reviews.name: Avi Kadu
featured_reviews.review_text:
First of all, gratitude to the owner for working towards the development of the society. I have also read your personal journey, and it is truly inspiring to see where you started and what you have built today.
However, I would like to share my honest feedback about the food quality and service, which was disappointing during our visit.
I ordered a coffee, but it was not hot. I finished it quietly without creating any issue; you may even check the CCTV if required. However, proper serving temperature should be ensured.
We ordered a chicken omelette with cheese, but honestly, it was difficult to find the chicken in it. Initially, I thought there might be chunks inside, but there were no visible shreds or proper quantity. That was quite disappointing.
We also ordered nachni pancakes, and the dish was served with cold caramel sauce that seemed straight from the fridge.
Ideally, the server should inform whether the sauce will be served on the side or on top. Warm pancakes with apple and caramel sauce should not be cold, as it completely spoils the taste of the dish.
When the bill came, the lady at the counter suggested we need not pay due to the experience. However, we respect your effort and the noble work you are doing, so we chose to pay.
Sir, basic training for the chef and kitchen team is necessary. My child is autistic, and after waiting patiently for quite some time, receiving such food was disappointing for us. Eventually, we left the place dissatisfied.
I must mention that the server was good and well-trained, but he was slightly pushy while promoting initiatives. Sometimes this can irritate guests, so a balanced approach would help.
Please understand that we are genuine food lovers and not here to damage anyone’s reputation. We appreciate your noble work and truly hope you continue doing it. Just focus a little more on food quality, serving standards, and taste, and the place can become even better.
✅ Suggested Next Step:
If you want, I can also create a shorter, sharper Google review (more impactful and slightly aggressive) which usually gets faster attention from restaurant management.

featured_reviews.name: Stephen Antu Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved this place! The ambience is calm, welcoming, and has a beautiful vibe that instantly makes you feel at ease. I tried the Pink Sauce Pasta and the Spanish Omelette—the food was really good and well-prepared.

The service was handled by Jyoti (I hope I’ve got the name right—referring to the tall girl who also models), and she was excellent throughout. There was a small glitch in service because of which we couldn’t fully enjoy the Spanish Omelette, but Kushboo handled the feedback very gracefully. The way she spoke about the café’s story and its origin was truly inspiring.

It’s not just a café—it’s a place with a heart. Definitely worth visiting, especially to hear the story from Kushboo herself.

I’m giving one star less only because there’s room for improvement in the service, which I’m sure can be fixed with a little bit of training.

featured_reviews.name: Shifa Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Shubham Greens for lunch today. The restaurant is famous for it's authentic South Indian cuisines.
We ordered-
▪️Cheese Sada Dosa
▪️Mendu Wada

The Cheese Sada Dosa had the apt amount of cheese with crisp dosa. Whereas, the Mendu wada was quite tasty served with sambar and chutney.

featured_reviews.name: Abdullah Nore
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have visited multiple Baba Falooda branches over the years — Mahim, Crawford Market, and Andheri — and I always had a small request: please don’t add extra sugar syrup because my dad has diabetes and I personally prefer less sweetness. Every branch always understood and respected this request.

Recently at the Crawford Market branch, I even requested them to customize my order a little differently. Personally, I feel the regular increment-only flavours are subpar, while the kulfi-mix flavours like Green Pista and Malai Top taste much better — they’re just a bit too sweet for me. So I requested them not to add the Malai Kulfi or Pista Kulfi in those faloodas and instead make the base more ice-cream focused. The staff politely informed me that the taste would change, but I was completely fine with that, and honestly, I ended up liking it much more that way. The staff at these branches have always been polite, understanding, and delightful.

Today, however, I visited the Kurla branch of Baba Falooda, and the experience was extremely disappointing. Since it was a new branch for me, I was excited to try it and thought I would continue visiting this branch every year like the others.

Initially, the staff seemed ready to accommodate my request, but one staff member behaved very unprofessionally and refused, saying it was “more work.” That attitude was upsetting. People have different health conditions and taste preferences — some have diabetes, some prefer less sugar — and every other Baba Falooda branch has always understood this simple request except the Kurla branch.

I was extremely hungry at the time, but the rude and egoistic behavior of that staff member completely spoiled the experience for me. This review is being posted because I’m speaking about Baba Falooda as a franchise overall. After today’s experience, I genuinely do not feel like visiting any Baba Falooda branch again.

featured_reviews.name: Md. Farhan Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a dessert lover in Mumbai, Baba Falooda is an absolute must-visit! The place is famous for its rich and refreshing faloodas that perfectly balance sweetness, texture, and flavor. The falooda comes loaded with creamy kulfi, silky vermicelli, basil seeds, and generous scoops of ice cream, making every bite incredibly satisfying.
What makes Baba Falooda special is the authentic taste and generous portion size. The kulfi is dense and flavorful, and the combination with rose syrup and chilled milk creates a dessert that’s both refreshing and indulgent. Despite being extremely popular and often crowded, the service is quick and efficient.
Whether you go after dinner or just to satisfy a sweet craving, Baba Falooda never disappoints. It’s one of those iconic Mumbai dessert spots that truly lives up to the hype.

featured_reviews.name: Ashish Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried a few flavors at Baba Falooda recently. The Mango, Malai, and Pista faloodas were all delicious—rich, flavorful, and definitely worth ordering. I'd recommend sticking to Mango, Malai, or Pista and giving the Black Currant a miss.
Overall, a great spot for a refreshing falooda fix!

featured_reviews.name: Manish Dhanavade
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐ (for Jogeshwari) | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (for Mahim)

Having had an excellent experience at Baba Falooda, Mahim, I was excited to try their new branch in Jogeshwari, but unfortunately, it was quite disappointing. The experience was not even 50% of what Mahim offers.

The ice cream and kulfi quality and quantity were not up to the mark, lacking the rich, creamy texture that Baba Falooda is known for. The dry fruits were sparse, and the overall falooda felt ordinary rather than indulgent. The taste, richness, and generosity that define the Mahim outlet were clearly missing.

Mahim continues to set a very high benchmark with its creamy, rich falooda and generous toppings, but the Jogeshwari branch has a long way to go to match that standard. I genuinely hope they improve consistency across outlets, because the brand name carries strong expectations.

Recommendation:
For the true Baba Falooda experience, Mahim is still the place to go. Jogeshwari needs significant improvement in quality, quantity, and overall execution.

featured_reviews.name: Sonam Karani
featured_reviews.review_text: I went to this place to taste the famous falooda and it was totally worth it . The portion and quality is very good . We ordered the famous baba falooda one by two portions and it was sufficient between three people to have . A seating arrangement around the place would make it more comfortable as an experience for people who go to have it and prefer having it while they  sit and relax. Rest all is worth it .
